document_check.note: Buawangpong N, Aramrat C, Pinyopornpanish K, et al. Risk Prediction Performance of the Thai Cardiovascular Risk Score for Mild Cognitive Impairment in Adults with Metabolic Risk Factors in Thailand. Healthcare 2022;10:1959. The cited 82.7% figure, MoCA < 25 definition and metabolic-risk outpatient setting are all present (348/421 = 82.7%).

cited_result: Prevalence of MCI of 82.7% (348 of 421), with MCI defined solely as a MoCA score below 25, among adults aged 45 or over with at least one metabolic risk factor attending outpatient clinics of Maharaj Nakorn Chiang Mai Hospital. The TCVR model discrimination (AUROC 0.58 to 0.61), which is the study's main aim, is not cited.
tool_reason: The review cites the study's MCI prevalence estimate, not its prediction-model performance, so the JBI prevalence checklist fits the cited result.

domains.domain: Item 1: Sample frame appropriate to address the target population
domains.rationale: The frame is the metabolic-risk outpatient clinics of one university hospital. That suits a clinic population but not the stated target of Thai adults with metabolic risks, and the document does not describe how the clinics relate to that wider population.

signalling.question: Was the sample frame appropriate to address the target population?
signalling.quote: The subjects were recruited from the outpatient clinics at Maharaj Nakorn Chiang Mai Hospital which provide care for patients with metabolic risks. These clinics included the family medicine clinic, general medicine clinic, endocrinology clinic, and cardiology clinic.

domains.rationale: The data pool a previous FGF21 study with additional data collected later. Consecutive or random sampling is not stated.

signalling.question: Were study participants sampled in an appropriate way?
signalling.quote: This study utilized data collected from a previous study examining the possible link between fibroblast growth factor 21 and cognitive decline among patients with metabolic risk factors [26]. Additional data were collected using a similar methodology for cardiovascular risk assessment and cognitive assessment to increase the sample size and power between 1 May 2020 and 31 May 2021.

domains.rationale: No sample-size calculation was done for the prevalence. Still, N = 421 with 348 cases gives a 95% CI of roughly 79% to 86% (my calculation from the reported counts), which is adequate precision.

signalling.question: Was the sample size adequate?
signalling.quote: From a total of 421 participants, 348 participants had MCI.

domains.domain: Item 4: Subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: The paper reports the inclusion criteria, clinic types, study period and Table 1 characteristics.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: We included patients 45 years old or over with at least one metabolic risk factor ... The majority of patients were female (63.66%) and obese (55.58%).

domains.domain: Item 5: Data analysis with sufficient coverage of the identified sample
domains.rationale: Every eligible patient had a MoCA score (Table 1 shows 0 missing), and all of them enter the prevalence.

signalling.question: Was the data analysis conducted with sufficient coverage of the identified sample?
signalling.quote: From a total of 421 eligible patients, there were 348 MCI and 73 non-MCI.

domains.domain: Item 6: Valid methods for identification of the condition
domains.rationale: MCI was identified only by a screening-test cut-off. The paper records no cognitive complaint, no functional assessment and no clinical or consensus diagnosis, so the method does not validly identify MCI. The authors state this as a limitation.

signalling.question: Were valid methods used for the identification of the condition?
signalling.quote: MCI was indicated by an MoCA score of less than 25. ... First, the diagnosis of MCI was based solely on the questionnaire.

signalling.question: Was the cut-off applied a diagnostic criterion rather than a screening threshold?
signalling.quote: MoCA is the standard tool for screening patients who have MCI. ... The maximum score is 30 and the cut-off score is 24/25 [28]. A score lower than 25 indicates MCI.

domains.domain: Item 7: Condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all participants
domains.rationale: All participants took the MoCA with the same cut-off. However, the two data-collection phases used only a 'similar' methodology. Rater training and any education correction are not reported.

signalling.question: Was the condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all participants?
signalling.quote: Additional data were collected using a similar methodology for cardiovascular risk assessment and cognitive assessment

signalling.question: Was the administration of the MoCA (raters, education adjustment) described?
signalling.quote: Searched for rater, training, administration and education adjustment of the MoCA; none reported.

domains.rationale: The prevalence appears only in the Discussion as a crude proportion. Numerator and denominator can be recovered (348/421), but no confidence interval is given.

signalling.question: Was there appropriate statistical analysis?
signalling.quote: In our sample, the prevalence of MCI among patients with metabolic risks was as high as 82.7 percent.

domains.rationale: The paper does not report how many patients were approached or how many declined.

signalling.question: Was the response rate adequate, and if not, was the low response rate managed appropriately?
signalling.quote: Searched for number approached, declined, response or participation rate; only the eligible total (421) is reported.

overall: High risk of bias (JBI prevalence; item 6, valid identification of the condition, is No)
overall_rationale: The review's JBI rule rates a study high when valid outcome measurement is No. Here the condition was identified by a single MoCA < 25 screening cut-off with no clinical MCI criteria (item 6 No). Sampling, measurement consistency, the precision reported and the response rate are also unclear.

applicability.rationale: The 82.7% counts MoCA screen-positives, not clinically diagnosed MCI. The review's own framing ('single-instrument ascertainment', 'MCI prevalence' in quotation marks) is consistent with this.
